newsitem.title: USA: Ashland offers $12.50 for Melamine shares.
newsitem.headline: Ashland offers $12.50 for Melamine shares.

text.p: Melamine Chemicals Inc on Monday said it received an unsolicited proposal from Ashland Inc, one of its principal stockholders, to buy shares it did not already own for $12.50 cash each.
Melamine Chairman James Crook said the offer "came as a surprise" and that the company's board would review and respond to the proposal "over the next several weeks."
Ashland curently owns 23.1 percent or 1.275 million shares of the company, a leading producer of a chemical called melamine, used in adhesives, laminates, paints and other products.
Ashland's bid values Melamine at about $69 million.
Melamine said Ashland, a U.S. energy and chemicals concern, had requested a response by July 17 and that the offer was subject to due diligence and other conditions.

Melamine, which is developing new melamine process and application technology, posted net earnings of $1.28 million for its third fiscal quarter that ended March, up from $780,000 in the year-earlier period. Sales for the latest quarter were $15 million, unchanged from the comparable quarter in 1996.
